strings.TBA_fascism_party_long: Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las Juntas de Ofensiva Nacional Sindicalista
strings.TBA_Rafael_Alvarez_hog_desc:
Chairman of the Council of Ministers
Socialism
--------------
Rafael Fernández Álvarez was a member of the Interprovincial Council of Asturias during the Civil War, and so it was an easy decision to nominate Fernández for the position of Speaker of the Council, given his experience in wartime politics. Within the position of Speaker of the Council of Government, Fernández wields power equivalent to that of a prime minister.

Fernández is a deeply influential member of the Asturian Socialist Federation, the local branch of the PSOE, however he is not its leader. Using his connections, he has established contact with the PSOE in the Republic, but the party's inner turmoil has given him pause. It puts the very future of Asturias into question: If they are to drop their arms and reintegrate into the Republic, would the post-war leadership truly be willing to make the changes necessary to allow Asturias to prosper, given their current division?
strings.TBA_Manuel_Mondelo_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Socialism
--------------
Manuel Mondelo Ronda was one of the leaders of the 1962 Asturias miner strikes, forced to go into hiding until the Union collapsed into civil war. Alongside his work as a miner, Mondelo was also a member of the Asturian Socialist Federation, as well as one of its leaders. When the time came for Asturias to rise up, Mondelo was nominated as Councilor of Foreign Affairs.

Given the circumstances of Asturias, the role of Councilor of Foreign Affairs was not a busy one, although it does still bear important responsibilities. Mondelo has reached out to leftist movements within the other regional factions, and has established talks with the Republic. Whale there is a common enemy to unite them, it is Mondelo's top priority to establish what will happen between the Republic and Asturias after the war's conclusion.
strings.TBA_Felipe_Matarranz_sec_desc:
Minister of the Armed Forces
Communism
--------------
Felipe Matarranz, known by the alias of El Lobo amongst his fellow guerrillas, had been fighting against fascism in Spain since before the Civil War. He was eventually captured, and narrowly avoided execution. However, Matarranz continued his fight against fascism after the civil war, getting into contact with other Asturian rebels and the PCE, and waging a violent resistance within the rugged mountains of the region. Now that the Union has collapsed, and the fascists are finally vulnerable, Matarranz has once again taken up arms to defend Asturias.

Named Councilor of Defense, Matarranz has used his knowledge of the mountainous Asturian terrain to better coordinate the militias, providing knowledge of optimal places to hide, and what routes the enemy is likely to take.
strings.TBA_Amaro_Rosal_eco_desc:
Minister of Economic Organization
Bukharinism
--------------
Amaro del Rosal had originally been a member of the PSOE, and had long been under the belief that it would benefit the party to collaborate alongside the communists in the PCE. In 1946, this position saw him evicted from the party while in exile, and so he joined the PCE in 1948. Despite this new affiliation, however, Amaro del Rosal remained a moderate within the PCE. It was for this reason that he was appointed Councilor of Economy, as he could act as a neutral candidate that both factions were willing to accept.

As Councilor, Amaro del Rosal has nationalized several key industries and mines, greatly expanding the rights of the workers. Using those same workers' output as a source of revenue, the government s able to keep its militias equipped and able to continue the fight for Asturias's future.
strings.TBA_a_new_red_spark_desc:
The whirlwinds of history rise once more and today, the stars shine upon us - the workers of Asturia.

It was a long and arduous journey to reach where we are today, and many of us are still uncertain of the future to tread. After all, our goals were never an independent Asturias, but our goals would never be fulfilled with any of the others around us.

Nevertheless, it is nothing less than clear that we, the workers and peasants of Asturias, are going to walk this path to the future, alone.

Of course, if we are to protect the home of the Asturian revolution, we must arm the workers from the murderous Spanish fascists beyond the frontiers. Even the darkest of nights will end in a bright red sunrise, of course.
strings.TBA_a_new_red_spark_tt: Asturias prefiere morir de pie a vivir de rodillas
strings.TBA_total_peoples_defense_desc:
We have the the support of the workers across Asturia and our nature certainly makes us popular to the workers of the surrounding regions, but it would be silly to expend any efforts and valuable manpower venturing beyond our lands, when we have Asturian workers to house, feed, and most importantly - protect.

Let us orient our efforts to maintain our defensive positions. After all, the original goal of our Republic was to protect the workers, and we are certainly not in any position to make expansive conquests in the face of our circumstances.
strings.TBA_the_revolutionary_council_desc:
Few of us remember the Sovereign Council of Asturias and León which existed during the Civil War, but many of us know of its feats as a great anti-fascist resistance movement against Franco's thugs.

Today, however, as history repeats itself, so too are we to take a page from the Civil War. The Asturian Revolutionary Council will play the vanguard role in leading the workers of Asturias towards the defence of the workers and construction of socialism in Asturia. The PCE and PSOE have begun playing a role in its foundation, though some independents have come forth to take the responsibility of being members. WIth further efforts to support their role in Asturian society, we can truly assert ourselves as being a government by, of and for the workers!
strings.TBA_booby_traps_desc:
Asturias is a land heavily defined by its coastal cliffs and mountainous frontiers - difficult to traverse for any military though nonetheless vulnerable if insufficiently defended.

Obviously we cannot enforce total coverage of our borders, but we can make as many deterrences from subjugation as possible. Reports indicate Fascist supply routes and caravans which cross into or detour in Asturian lands, suggesting even potential Fascist infiltration into our territory. If we were to rig traps along the exterior of Asturias which the military will tread upon, we can simultaneously delay the possibility of larger offensives into Asturias as well as potentially grab some equipment from unsuspecting Fascist convoys.
strings.TBA_raid_their_supply_lines_desc:
While we have oriented our efforts towards bunkering down and defending the regions of Asturia, for the fruits they have bore us in defending ourselves from exterior threats, economically and logistically it has pushed us towards destruction.

One way or another, the blood must continue to flow. Thankfully, the Fascists' war machine demonstrates an immense wealth in the same supplies we are lacking in - and every now and then they venture not too far from roads which lie close enough to our borders for us to... Intervene and repurpose, to put it simply. For this reason it would be a wise decision to set up raid parties with the purpose of crossing the border in search of convoys and stashes which we can attack, disrupting the logistics of our enemies and putting the fruits of the workers' labours back in our own hands.
strings.TBA_breaking_the_chains_desc:
Across the mountains and fields of Asturia, one million workers cry out in despair from the looming threat of the murderous, oppressive Fascists.

At least, this would be the reality were we not to take up arms and defend ourselves, and it certainly will be much worse than this if we are to fail our mission to defend the Asturian workers and peasants. Our people must be made to understand this as reality, and must be convinced to rally together to defend our future. Thus, we will initiate a complex and extensive propaganda campaign to ensure the loyalty and cooperation of the people so that not only will they understand the matter of the situation we are in, but they will us in this national struggle.
strings.TBA_introduce_military_commissars_desc:
Though our militias are comprised of the once-oppressed Asturian workers who dare to take up arms to defend their homes, Fascist infiltrators have begun to show their ugly heads, spawning demagogues, swindlers, and even partisans who have deceived our men and even caused great disruption within the army itself.

We can take a note from the pages of history and combat this using political commissars, who will ensure the ideological loyalty of our militiamen and keep the army in check, lest the fascist ideas and deviants start to take root in the army.
strings.TBA_total_committal_to_the_revolution_de:
The accomplishments of our last propaganda efforts have demonstrated an immense loyalty to our cause from the people, but it simply is not enough. We demand nothing less than total commitment to the Revolution, and we will once again appeal to the people to win their support.

Some will criticise our decisions to further repress and ask more of our people, likening us to the Germans who brought upon their people a “Total War” which brought upon their victory in the last Great War. This is simply a mistaken or even deceptive perspective, one that slanders us by likening us to the Fascists we are trying to resist.

Our full commitment to the Revolution is predicated on the total defeat of the Fascists, and we must not falter in any effort to put up a valiant resistance.
strings.TBA_take_the_fight_to_the_sky: Take the Fight to the Sky
strings.TBA_take_the_fight_to_the_sky_desc:
When the Fascists last rampaged across Spain, with the support of the dark Germanic hordes their black wings smothered the skies and dominated the air. It was clear that in the victory the fascists achieved in the Civil War, the superiority of the Fascists' air power paved the way to their total domination of Spain.

We are not inclined to make the same mistake that cost the Republicans' the future of Spain. In order to ensure that we do not fall the same way, we will draft and organise at least a small air force to defend the Asturian skies and chase away the bombs of the Fascists. We cannot yet make any effort to use them for raids outside Asturia, but we can at the very least defend ourselves from aerial attacks and bombing runs which would choke the chimneys of our factories and burn the life out of our cities.
strings.TBA_the_red_motor_brigades_desc:
With the defensive situation around Asturias having shown immense success, let us now move towards preparing increased offensives to protect the periphery of Asturias too.

Motor brigades, consisting of motorised vehicles supported by infantry and artillery, move fast and hit hard, like the sharpened head of a spear - making them the ideal candidate to move in the front of an offensive thrust, hence being named a “spearhead”. The increased offensive operations will require the creation and training of new motor brigades - the Red Motor Brigades. With the captured equipment from the Fascists and the weapons caches and arsenals in Asturias, we can certainly make a headstart on the development of these new brigades.
strings.TBA_the_young_revolutionaries_desc:
Some thirty years ago, as we all know, the Civil War was lost, and those who were not managed to settle down and make new lives for themselves even under the black wings of the Fascist regime. Those men and women bore children, in secret instilling in them the ideals and beliefs that made us human, giving them the dignity that the Fascists had stripped from everyone.

Today, those children have grown up and have even bore children of their own, passing the same words from their parents on to their children - and now has come the ultimate test to show exactly to what extent those lessons of their parents were learnt. Many young Asturians have joined in the revolution and are ready to lay down their lives for the future so cruelly taken from them thirty years ago. We must take note and see to it that their fervour and passion are not wastefully expended.
strings.TBA_the_party_vanguard_desc:
It was once only a rumour that the people who once fought in the Civil War and managed to continue their lives even under the Fascist regime still lingered among the households of Iberia, waiting for the right time to bring about the destruction of the jackboot that has oppressed us for several decades.

Showing their faces now in the midst of this bloody end of Iberia, as the prophecy foretold they have now made ready to take up arms in valiant resistance. The veterans of the PCE and PSOE, ideologically and militarily hardened from their prior experience, are precisely what Asturias needs at the helm of fighting the Fascists and preserving the Revolution. One of the first to fight, we are ready to make them one of the first to lead, too.
strings.TBA_leading_from_the_front_desc:
It is often a criticism that war is nothing but young men dying fighting for bitter old men - and that while soldiers are sacrificing their lives in horrific conditions those in charge live comfortably, stuffing their faces with luxury foods while the soldiers live off rations. While this may be true for the feudal and capitalist states and the Fascists we are fighting, it simply isn't true of us, and we are dedicated to make a point of this.

We will have the leadership regularly visit the front, showing support for the troops in person and demonstrating to even our enemies that our leaders can put their lives where their mouths are. Obviously, putting our leaders in fighting positions could prove to be disastrous, but their mere appearances at the barracks and headquarters are sure to motivate the soldiers.
strings.TBA_funding_the_struggle_desc:
Like any engine must run on petrol or diesel, the Revolution requires a strong economy and access to even more resources to keep itself running. Neglecting something so vital that it makes the lifelines and bloods of the beating heart that is the Asturian Revolution would prove to be a fatal mistake - one that we know better than to make.

To ensure that our struggle lives on to see the sun rise each day, we will make a dedicated effort to not only jumpstart but keep the Asturian economy fruitful even through these turbulent times that define the Revolution. Keeping Asturians well-fed will secure their support and perpetuate their dedication to our cause, ready to both fight and build more weapons.
strings.TBA_liquidate_private_assets_desc:
Our efforts to bolster the Asturian economy have been resoundingly successful, but it isn't the only source of income left untapped. Asturias while under the central control of the Iberian Union housed the assets of several prominent Fascist organisations and businesses - all of which have fled or are otherwise incapacitated to resist any effort of ours to seize them.

In more ways than one, this is a golden opportunity to strengthen our efforts to grow our economic output. Everything useful can be allocated straight to the fight against the Fascists, while that which cannot shall be liquidated directly into the reserves.
strings.TBA_a_call_to_the_world_desc:
There is no need for us to stand alone when Internationalism has always been one of the cornerstones of the left and the world does not lack comrades who would be eager to aid us in our cause if only we asked them for help in these desperate times.

The time has come to spread the word far and wide that Asturias calls upon all friends of communism around the globe to once again take up the cause of antifascism in Iberia in any way they can so that our red bastion can survive the oncoming onslaught.
strings.TBA_guns_of_the_revolution_desc:
Karl Marx once wrote about the necessity of arming the workers, a wisdom we must heed now at all costs lest we be crushed in this war and the forces of reaction are free to bring about another dark age on this land.

We will arm ourselves with whatever is available when modern firearms are scarce, everything from museum pieces from the First Civil War to old rifles from the days of 1934, anything that can shoot a bullet will have to suffice so that we are not completely helpless.
strings.TBA_socialize_the_economy_desc:
The necessities of war prevent us from being able to implement our full program just yet, but that is no excuse not to prepare for that inevitability as the urgency of the situation gives us leeway when it comes to reorganizing the economy.

We will begin to take steps toward moving past bourgeois control over the means of production and rationalizing our agro-industrial capacity to serve the needs of the people better and prepare it for handover to the workers soon.
strings.TBA_industrial_seizures_desc:
It is abundantly clear that the days of the bourgeoisie are numbered in the society we are building even if the needs of war kept us from seizing all private industry when we started. But now the war effort needs to be expanded and such allowances only hinder us.

To that end, we will seize any private industry that remains within our republic and place it in the hands of the workers, loyal to our cause and unbound by the logic of the so-called free market and allowing our industry to be rationalized and directed towards seeing this war to its end.
strings.TBA_revolution_in_the_universities_desc:
Isn't it beautiful?

What was once a whisper in the caves and mineshafts of Avilés, now made its way through the streets of Gijón and into the hearts and minds of the youth! Isn't there nothing more satisfying than seeing the youth, the bringers of new revolutionary thought and fervour, take up arms and join our cause?

These younger revolutionaries may be inexperienced with arms, but the tenacity of their devotion to our movement cannot remain unexamined. Perhaps, with the right ideological teachings, they too will lead the next generation of bright, profound socialist thought.
strings.TBA_the_miners_due_desc:
What keeps the lifeline of the Asturian economy, and thereby the rest of the country, from destruction and chaos? The answer to this question can be found from a simpler one: Where does revolutionary thinking find itself most manifest?

The industry, particularly our large mining sector have always been something we pride ourselves on since the days of the Union - though tense relations strained the cooperation between the administration and the workers themselves, culminating in a significant degree of political and social repression, they have made it abundantly clear that they are interested in a socialist reorganisation. Perhaps by listening to their complaints about their previous conditions, making mines safer and increasing wages, we can win over their support.
strings.TBA_expand_unions_powers_desc:
The party is the backbone of any socialist project but the hard truth is that it can't do everything by itself nor can it be everywhere at once, at least not without becoming something warped beyond its ideals. However, it is good to remember that we are not alone in this struggle.

The UGT and CCOO have long stood by us as allies and comrades in the long struggle against reaction, it is only natural that we begin to entrust them with more responsibilities as our government expands its scope and surely they will be interested in bolstering their and our presence in every workplace in the region.
strings.TBA_prioritize_gun_production_desc:
Building socialism was never going to be easy, it is a path fraught with danger and demands sacrifice so that the flame of the workers' revolution is not snuffed out by the flood of reaction that rises against us every time without fail.

Thus it is regrettable but necessary that the civilian economy will have to take a back seat as priority shifts to producing as many guns as there are people to carry them and then some so that we can fight back against those who would put us in chains again. We can only hope those we fight for understand the need for this.
strings.TBA_fortify_oviedo_desc:
With Spain once again racked by the onslaught of Civil War, echoes of the 1936 conflict have been quick to reappear as the battlelines begin to form. To the northwest of Iberia sits the ancient city of Oviedo, once a stronghold of the Carlists of yesteryear and now a bastion for the reincarnated nation of Asturias.

With the chances of Asturian independence from the now fractious states of Spain already dubious, defense in depth is the only real offense we have in our arsenal. By fortifying the city and surrounding area against inevitable Spanish invasion, we will be better able to bleed Madrid white until Asturias' sovereignty has been firmly secured.
strings.TBA_keeping_the_people_satisfied_desc:
Our revolution is about more than just mere survival. Survival was all we did before and if that becomes our sole focus then we are doomed to repeat the mistakes of those who came before us and are no better than the capitalists we overthrew.

Though this will mean less military equipment and limit the war effort, we will prioritize the production of civilian goods to meet the people's needs and maintain their morale in this trying time. Though this will earn us much goodwill, we hope it does not weaken us so much that all is lost.
strings.TBA_vanguards_of_the_revolution_desc:
For too long the people of Iberia have been left alone in the despair and horror of the dual-Fascist regime. For near 30 long, gruesome and bloody years the masses have been left to wallow in the decay of despotic Fascism, a heinous ideology held aloft by the loathsome reactionary figures of Franco and Salazar. Now though, they can finally breathe a moment of reprieve as the Asturian Workers' Battalion has arisen to take the fight to the Fascist menace. We are the material reality of the people's will, the very convention of their attitudes through the means of popular armed struggle and the protectors of the great revolution. Whilst the bourgeois collaborator, the Falangist filth and the bureaucratic entities of the Fascist state once rested easy in their mansions, the BTA shall now arise to put the scare into these reactionaries. The Fascists built their power on the blood of the working class but we will now hit back twice as hard in what is to be a glorious prolonged struggle. The Fascist will know the anger of working-class rage, they shall feel the fury of popular willpower and the letters “BTA” shall be inscribed into their cursed minds as a real-life boogeyman. We are here, comrades, to accomplish at least one key objective. To take our vengeance for decades of tyranny and murder.

“We have no compassion and we ask no compassion from you...we shall not make excuses for the terror.” - Karl Marx
strings.TBA_vanguards_of_the_revolution_tt: We are the one true champions of the revolution.
strings.TBA_venceremos_desc:
A few years ago such a thing would have been deemed impossible, a fantasy even! But against all odds, we have not only survived but thrived and our revolution has grown from a mere candle's flame to an inferno that has burned away the darkness of reaction across the land.

Victory against the fascists is now closer than ever before and an end to the nightmare is within our sights. We must press onwards now and everyone must keep contributing to the war effort as we race to the finish line in this race for survival, so that we may finally be free of this damnable war.
strings.TBA_memories_34_desc:
While the better part of three decades might have since gone by, echoes of the Revolución de 1934 still ring high among those comrades that found themselves or their relatives thrown into the chaos of October's uprising.

Then, too, were workers rising up against Madrid's increasingly fascist regime to fight for their rights and those of their peers. And just as today, Asturias was at the forefront of the struggle.

Now, callbacks to the two thousand souls that perished from the subsequent reactionary repression spread far and wide as a rallying cry to the militias of now.

Never again.
strings.TBA_uncertain_future_desc:
If few things are more certain than the righteousness of the workers' collective front against fascism, the matter of what comes after the struggle is another riddle entirely.

The truth is that independent sentiment is far from unanimous among the people of Asturias. Yet, the option of joining the liberals of the Spanish Republic doesn't hold much sway either, leaving the question of the future tossed aside while focus is maintained on the front lines.

As the protracted conflict further pushes the provisional regime to exceed the means of its hastily formed institutions, this puzzle might find itself in need of solving much sooner than anticipated. And as long as the interim government stays reluctant to pick a clear stance, all paths remain seemingly open for the young republic.
strings.TBA_wars.1.d:
“I will be stuck in here forever, aren't I?” Carlos groaned as he watched his partner Manuel ineffectually try and get him out of the pit he fell into, a fate he could have avoided if Manuel hadn't been so distracted enjoying the sound of his voice that he failed to notice the gaping hole that now imprisoned Carlos.

“This is not working, Carlos. The hole is too deep for me to get you out. I will go back to camp and get help. You stay put here, okay?” The bumbling idiot said before he ran off.

“As if I could just walk away for a stroll, can't believe I got stuck with him.” Carlos angrily muttered as he wondered what he had ever done in his life to get stuck on patrol with such a waste of space, a man who only got anywhere near a uniform because daddy was some decorated officer who made it happen. And now he and other capable soldiers had to baby him around, and now. instead of finishing his patrol and retiring for a well-earned rest. he was trapped in this...

His thoughts paused, and his anger was now interlaced with contemplation. He was trapped in a literal sense as he looked around and realized this pit had dimensions perfect for trapping a person in but also leaving the possibility of extraction later - far too perfect for it to be natural. It was a trap but who set it?

He suspected he would know the answer soon as he heard careful footsteps approaching his position, and his darkness-adjusted eyes managed to make out three armed figures who were not his comrades staring down at him.
strings.TBA_wars.2.d:
Arlo had once heard that famine victims could die from overeating once food was available again. He didn't think much of this knowledge until now as he took his first steps outside the prison he thought would be his tomb as he spent years behind bars - his only crime was being a PCE member. His first taste of freedom in years was as frightening as it was exciting.

He had resigned himself to a slow death in that prison when the unexpected happened. The regime collapsed like a house of cards, causing Iberia to be swept by chaos and revolutions. One of those had seen him liberated from his cage and take his first steps outside that accursed building, taking in air that did not smell nauseating. The pleasure was momentary as his mind raced with questions it never had to consider for years: what does he do now? Where to go? Was there anyone he knew left on the outside after so long?

The last question was answered immediately, as he spotted two faces, one of whom moved towards him so fast he nearly flinched as she hugged him tight. Good to know Carmen was as strong as ever and even better to see his old comrade Juan crack one of his rare smiles as he looked at this impromptu reunion. There were tears shed, explanations told, and questions asked, but Arlo wanted one thing. “So Juan, think I can get me a place in the militia, Red Army, or whoever is fighting the fascists right now?” he asked and was not surprised to see befuddlement on their faces.

“It hasn't been a day, and you can hardly walk, let alone fight my friend. Maybe, it's best t...” Arlo shook his head and gave him a look.

“I will regain my strength on the march, I will cook, I will do anything I can, but I have lived through helplessness for years now, and I would rather die than live without purpose again...
strings.TBA_wars.3.d:
He expected anger, to be told he is a stupid boy wasting his life on things better left alone. He predicted a lot of pleading and begging to stay safe with his last remaining family. He was even ready for denial, and his grandfather simply pretending he never said a thing, going about everything like normal.

He was not ready when Abuelo simply sighed and gave him his blessing to join the militia, throwing the youth into confusion and deflating the bravado he mustered for this talk.

“You look surprised. I know what you are thinking, and this is not a trick. You are free to go and fight if that is what you truly want. I won't even make you promise to come back alive. That's not a promise anyone can keep, not in a war of all places”. He then stood up and for a moment, Manuel could swear his grandfather's age seemed to melt away.

“But if you are going to do this, then there is a lot you must learn first, and you will listen to everything I tell you from this point forward if you don't want to be deadweight when the shooting starts, understand?” he said with a tone that carried both authority and care.

“Yes, of course, Grandpa. I understand,” he said without thinking.

“Good, now what I tell you will not substitute for experience; you only get that through your successes and failures, but at least you won't be starting from scratch, which is more than I ever got when I was in your shoes,” he said with a mix of both nostalgia and bitterness. “And above all else..”
strings.TBA_wars.3.a: “...you will need luck, lots of it.”
strings.TBA_wars.4.d:
“What do you mean I am not allowed in?”

Antonio resisted the urge to roll his eyes out of professionalism as he stared at his former colleague Santiago and repeated what he said.

“Sorry friend, but the university library is closed and will remain so while the university's reorganization is ongoing.”

“Yes I heard you the first time and I do not understand why am I not allowed in, I need to access the library to finish my degree otherwise all the money and effort I put into this will be wasted. Come on Antonio, can't you let me in just this once?” he pleaded and Antonio found himself irritated at the fact that Santiago seemingly did not notice the reality that they were at war right now.

“The answer is still the same, the library is closed until the higher ups tell me otherwise. If you want something to do the university council or the militia could..” he didn't finish his sentence when he noticed his former study mate walk away in anger.

“Forget it damn you, I ain't interested in this nonsense. I came here to study not run around playing revolutionary hero”
strings.TBA_wars.5.d: Two Junta soldiers are patrolling the forest around a camp. One trips over a wire headfirst into a pit hidden by foliage. The other tries to get him out but the pit is too deep and he can't reach him. He shouts he is going to get help at the camp, leaving the fallen soldier alone. The now alone soldier scuffs and thinks how useless his partner is when a thought crosses his mind, who put this trap here? His tribulations are cut short when he sees three figures pointing guns at him from the top of the pit.
strings.TBA_wars.6.d: Two Junta soldiers are patrolling the forest around a camp. One trips over a wire headfirst into a pit hidden by foliage. The now alone soldier scuffs and thinks how useless his partner is when a thought crosses his mind, who put this trap here? His tribulations are cut short when he sees three figures pointing guns at him from the top of the pit.
strings.TBA_wars.7.d:
Dust hung in the air of the apartment, unable to settle as the room shook from nearby blasts of heavy ordinance. The lights, powered by a noisy and battered generator, flickered intermittently, plunging the makeshift HQ into darkness.

It had been unoccupied since before the War. White paint peeled off the walls like thin gray appendages, almost antique appliances that couldn't be thrown out remained fixed in their places. It was chosen at the spur of the moment, after direct hits buried the primary command post under twenty feet of rubble. This dingy apartment, bustling with demands and orders was almost all that was left of Oviedo Command. Most were buried with their post.

“General!” cried out a radio operator from the former bedroom. It could barely be heard over the racket of the apartment but its intended target registered it almost supernaturally. A gruff man, aged a decade older than he should be, shoved a cigarette into an overflowing ashtray on the dining room table. Apologizing for leaving to the throng of wide eyed soldiers, and for the blackened debris spilling onto the maps below the ashtray, he pushed his way into the other room.

The radio operator wasted no time in acknowledging his superior. “Urgent. The Ronda Sur Post is gone. Last message said if we don't move troops they'll overrun the east fast”

The General's hollow eyes seemed to stare into the radio for a moment. “Get the civilians out of the shelters, anyone who is able. Give them a weapon, anything that can kill, we need them.” he said briskly.

“Sir, is that...?”

The General turned and walked to the door. “There's no one else to send” he said, before pushing his way back into the other room.
strings.TBA_wars.7.a: The enemy was stalled for a few more hours.
strings.TBA_wars.12.d:
Pedro could feel his lungs burning with every step he made. He could barely feel his legs as the effort of keeping them in motion, and the pain that came with it, became such a constant his body simply became numb to it. But he could not stop to rest, to do so would be to let them catch him.

It wasn't supposed to be this way, not so long ago he was just a clerk and not even a very important one. He might have expressed some loud nationalist sentiments, sure, but everyone had to do that if they wanted to keep their jobs. Behind the Francoist slogans was just a pile of paperwork. He dealt with road maintenance, for God's sake. With this “revolution” however, the people had decided they had always been latent revolutionaries. Now he was a target as if he were some Guardia Civil specter.

He had been lucky to have already been outside his home when they tore into it, incensed by the proclamations on the radio that a new Socialist Asturias Republic had formed, and had even been luckier still to make it out of town. If he hadn't heard the announcement, noticed the glances the people on his street had given him recently, he wouldn't have known to run. The thought terrified him but even now he knew they were still pursuing him. The voices were not getting any quieter.

Suddenly, his legs failed and he felt dirt on his face as his muscles failed him and he fell down onto the rough ground. He could not stop panting even as he tried to stay still in the hopes they would miss his prone form.

Footsteps and the clinking of metal grew louder. Then, it stopped. He looked up.
strings.TBA_wars.12.a: They surrounded him, tools and bludgeons mockingly displayed.
strings.TBA_wars.13.t: Paper Makes the World Go Round
strings.TBA_wars.13.d:
“So many names, so little time” Armando said to himself as his eyes scanned yet another long list of arrests. Another round of purges meant more work for him to go through.

He wasn't ungrateful for his job. The birth of the Republic had allowed him to rise high, higher than he had dreamed, but he was now finding himself wondering if he was really suited for it. He forced himself to concentrate while sifting through the names, determining who was deserving of what punishment with a hasty scrawl. He sighed. The names never stopped

The only help he got was from his assistant Elena, who was efficient and dedicated he couldn't deny, but hardly the most socially adept or engaging person. A computer would have been more company, a thought that groaned through his head as she walked into his office, in her hands more lists for him to go through. He gasped as he saw them added to the already overflowing desk

“More of these?!” He slammed his desk in impotent frustration, causing some of the papers that had been precariously clinging to the piles to fall slowly to the ground. Elena picked them up silently and re-added them before him, eliciting an exasperated squeal from Armando. He stood up and walked to the wall, leaning on it as days of monotony welled to the surface.

“God, this is pointless!” he let out, “Can't they just shoot the bastards or something? How many police officers are even in this damned city?!” He felt his vein almost pop out from the frustration, so preoccupied that he didn't notice Elena nod and walk out to deliver his new order.
